title: Information Classification and Handling Policy
scope: This policy applies to information created, received, processed, stored, transmitted, or disposed of by the organization regardless of format, system, location, or custodian.
principles: Information is classified according to business impact, confidentiality, integrity, availability, privacy, contractual, and regulatory considerations.
The information owner is accountable for classification, handling requirements, access decisions, and periodic review.
Handling controls must be proportionate to the sensitivity and lifecycle risk of the information.
Information is retained only for a documented purpose and securely disposed of when the approved retention period ends.

requirements.statement: Every material information asset must have an accountable owner and an assigned classification before production use.
The organization must use the levels Public, Internal, Confidential, and Restricted with documented criteria for each level.
Confidential and Restricted information must use approved encryption and access controls during storage and transmission.
Access to Confidential and Restricted information must be limited to approved roles and reviewed by the information owner on a defined cadence.
External sharing of Confidential or Restricted information requires an approved purpose, recipient validation, and contractual or privacy safeguards where applicable.
Retention and secure disposal requirements must be documented for each classification and validated through periodic sampling.

exceptions.compensating_control: Limit the dataset, apply additional monitoring, and record the approved purpose and end date.
Block external transfer by default and use an approved secure exchange with additional review.
